notes: Direct HTTP fetch only (site fully reachable). Same Algolia setup as Bestsellers/New Arrivals. Enumerated the full 845-collection /collections.json export and keyword-scanned for clearance/outlet/sale/final/last-chance/end-of-line/discontinued -- NO collection anywhere on the site uses the words 'Clearance' or 'Outlet' in its handle or title (0 matches). The only markdown-merchandising taxonomy the site exposes is 'Sale'. Sale-vs-Clearance reasoning: /collections/sale has TITLE 'Sale Items + New Markdowns', H1 'Sale', meta description 'Shop final sale offers ... Find pieces you love at a price you won't want to miss', and its own top-nav parent menu item is headlined 'Labor Day Sale Up to 70% Off' -- an explicit, dated, limited-time campaign framing, not permanent-clearance/outlet framing. Searched the full page text for clearance/outlet/last chance/end of line/discontinued/permanent: 0 occurrences of every one of those. However the page DOES expose a per-product Algolia facet named meta.display.final_sale ('Final Sale') as a selectable refinement, meaning some (not all) items in the listing are individually flagged final-sale/non-returnable -- a genuine permanence signal mixed into an otherwise temporary-campaign-branded page. Because of this mixed signal (temporary-event branding dominant, but a real final-sale product facet present) the row is recorded per the brief's explicit instruction, flagged AMBIGUOUS rather than silently included or excluded. Site exposes genuine Sale sub-structure (Sale > Furniture/Rugs/Lighting/Decor+Tabletop/Pillows+Throws/Walls/Bed+Bath/Outdoor, all under the same 'Labor Day Sale' nav parent, each a distinct collection) but since the parent classification itself is unresolved, only the single parent 'Sale' row is recorded rather than expanding all 8 children into flagged rows too. Also inspected and excluded (not ambiguous, not recorded) as clearly temporary promotional campaigns rather than clearance/outlet: /collections/promotions (TITLE 'Labor Day Sale Event: Up to 25% Off', qty=4902 -- near-catalog-wide, a banner-eligibility tag collection, not a merchandised listing), /collections/labor-day-sale-event-up-to-25-off (same campaign, qty=35), /collections/sarah-sherman-samuel-sale (a single designer's temporary sale, qty=53). /collections/new-sale ('New On Sale', qty=287, identical nbHits to /collections/sale) was also inspected -- it is a filtered subset of the same Sale taxonomy (newly-added markdowns) rather than a separate concept, so it was not recorded as an additional row; if it is in fact a true alias of /collections/sale (same underlying listing) that supports treating them as one candidate rather than two, consistent with the identical count. Checked main nav mega menu, the /collections/sale page's own content, and the full collections.json export; site search was not additionally used since the taxonomy was already exhaustively enumerated via collections.json.

rows.flag: MANUAL REVIEW: AMBIGUOUS SALE/CLEARANCE - page is nav-branded and titled as a temporary/dated promotional sale ('Labor Day Sale Up to 70% Off', meta description mentions final sale offers with no returns implication) with zero occurrences of Clearance/Outlet/Last Chance/End of Line wording anywhere on the page, but it exposes a genuine per-product 'Final Sale' facet suggesting some items are permanently non-returnable markdowns rather than a purely seasonal event. Could not confirm with certainty whether the site's own taxonomy treats this as permanent clearance-style merchandising or a rotating promotional campaign; recorded per brief instruction rather than guessed either way.
